key_insight: Label-free persona and knowledge directions can detect deception in LLM activations, but their effectiveness depends on the model, lie type, and reply wording.
engineering_relevance: These activation-based directions offer a lightweight alternative to supervised lie-detection probes, but require model-specific and wording-controlled validation.
method: Expand an honest/deceptive persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they possess, and extract middle-layer persona directions.
Build a knowledge direction using answerable versus unanswerable questions followed by identical scripted denials.
Evaluate individual and summed directions against supervised probes and random-direction baselines.
evidence_signal: Across four models on Liars’ Bench, persona directions outperformed single-dataset probes on three, while summed persona and knowledge directions beat same-depth supervised probes on all four, with one comparison near chance.
watch_item: Persona directions often track wording rather than deception, and gains do not consistently transfer to identical-word denials or held-out lies.
paper_title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
